correctness.rationale: From the up/down flip rates, the odd binomial terms of [(1−m)(1+bm)^6−(1+m)(1−bm)^6]/64 give the stated drift. The independent update contributes −pm. The endpoints point inward; noncentral equilibria are the intersections of A_b(z) with 32p/(1−p) for 0<z<1. When b≤3/4, A_b decreases there (except the negative constant at b=0); when b>3/4 its derivative decreases strictly from positive at 0 to negative at 1. This proves the full root count, and the sign of zA_b′ fixes simple-root stability. At a nonzero tangency A_b″<0 and the p-derivative of the drift is nonzero, so it is a fold, not a two-sided attractor. At b=3/4+2δ the coefficients of z and z² are (45/2)δ+O(δ²) and −1701/512+O(δ), giving the fold displacement 640δ/189 and height gap (800/21)δ² to leading order. The derivative 128/5041 of the height-to-p map gives the width constant. Exact rational re-expansion of the flip rates gave the tricritical drift coefficients −1701/18176 and −729/145408 for m^5 and m^7; an independent multiplication in Q(√6) also checked the r=0 spinodal. The critical inverse-fourth-power and ordinary inverse-square growth rates follow by differentiating along sign-preserving solutions and taking time averages. The packaged checker was inspected, not executed; the proof is for the deterministic ODE with 0<p<1.

value.rationale: The smallest discontinuous signed group size is a motivated test case of the earlier homogeneous theory. The result replaces a numerically located off-center fold with an exact bistability interval and identifies its leading collapse and deterministic relaxation on the physical phase line.
